Not even close.

For example, a BMW X5 weighs about 2200 Kgs without passengers, and it's GVWR is 2800 Kgs.

children.author: starcast2026
children.text: Hope they don't remove this flag

There aren't any documented settings to disable this, but there is a feature flag it currently sits behind. You can flip it in your ~/.codex/config.toml[1]:

  [features]
  daemon_auto_start = false
There are also some files that it writes to in ~/.codex at startup: pid files, lock files, things like that. You can delete them and replace them with symlinks to /dev/null, then mark those unwritable with `chattr +i` or similar. Presumably then the background daemon will crash on startup, if the feature flag ever goes away.

children.author: TZubiri
children.text:
A brief story of these agentic harnesses, from the perspective of a dev that barely used them.

I remember when opencode was out, I installed it as a separate user and tried it and it was cool.

Then Copy.fail came out, and I worried that a separate user really wasn't enough, but I felt I was overworrying at this point.

Then it worked fine and I felt silly for going through the trouble of a separate user even.

Then the opencode guys started self developing the tool itself and it became slop, this was like 2 months into the fad, and it was clear the quality merited uninstalling the thing, even if it did some cool magic ( https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues?q=is%3Aissue+au... )

Then Codex came out, and uninstalling opencode became the optimal move, if only because it removes a third party. It's one of those things where people will continue to use it out of inertia (either legacy code, or people reading/watching old tutorials), like using Axios in 2026 after Fetch was made standard, or using Mono after Microsoft released multiplatform dotnet.

Everything was good for some time, but then it quickly became obvious that OpenAI wasn't developing this tool, but rather letting it build itself, which results in a lot of slop (High RAM usage, inefficient looping that only works out of sheer GPU power and tight token limits, resulting in Skinner-box based development)

Then I uninstalled Codex, but this Pi thing came out, from the authorship of the dude from Flask, but I'm tapping out here, then Jev came out and I'm just not playing this game, good luck to everyone who is using these things.

It feels like this is an attrition game where we are waiting for the bubble to pop, but the bubble is made very long to tempt people into taking the bait. I'm betting the house on the day of reckoning, and hope that those that didn't take the AI bait, (or took the AI pill and repented) will be one of the few players left with a reputation.

I remember going in interviews and people asking me if I could use these tools, they wanted to see what projects I made, but I wasn't comfortable even showing a Chess Engine thing, like I didn't make this, this is not what I'm going to be delivering professionally, I'd rather be unemployed for a couple of months or years if that's what it takes, I'm not vibecoding for a salary sorry.
